headline: Palantir posts a first $2B+ quarter with revenue up 96%; Anthropic IPO, Marvell-Lumentum and Qwen-for-Apple stay in play

threads.title: Anthropic's IPO filing and the race to fund the frontier labs
threads.now: Anthropic filed its S-1 and could list on Nasdaq as soon as November, possibly raising about $100B at a $1.5T to $2T valuation. The amended filing shows Q3 revenue of $16.96B, nine-month revenue of $33.2B, compute at 58% of revenue and $895B of purchase and lease commitments, $447B due before 2030. Adjusted operating income was $2.5B.
threads.changed: Amended S-1 filed Nov 2: Q3 revenue $16.96B but a $567M operating loss versus a $974M profit in Q2, after $5B of pricey short-term compute. Risk language says future models may "imminently" hit its AI-accelerated-progress threshold.
threads.watch: Roadshow launch and price range; what safeguards Anthropic says its acceleration-threshold language triggers, including any Responsible Scaling Policy update.

history.change: Anthropic S-1 digested on Hard Fork and Decoder; FT reportedly says OpenAI shrank its round to about $20B at $1.25T.
20VC adds Meta's reported equity raise and the scale of Anthropic's planned issuance.
All-In transcript: capital-efficiency reading of the S-1, a smaller needed raise, 250 customers above $10M, and open-source commoditization named as the top risk.
Latent Space episode frames the IPO as about two weeks away at roughly $2T.
Big Technology transcript adds S-1 detail: revenue growth, customer diversification, compute-efficiency chart and compute risk factor.
Amended S-1: Q3 revenue $16.96B, operating loss $567M, $895B compute commitments, and new warning that the acceleration threshold may be near.

threads.title: AI capex boom meets a market selloff: cloud earnings, Vertiv and the chip rout
threads.now: Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7B; Microsoft Cloud hit $63.9B. Amazon says AWS grew over 39%. Alphabet says Gemini APIs process nearly 32 billion tokens a minute and holds 2026 capex at $195B to $205B. Thursday Intel fell 28.6% and the chip index about 7%.
threads.changed: On All-In, hosts said Alphabet shares fell 10% to 15% Thursday, erasing about $500B, on search ad-click worries, even as Google Cloud operating profit passed $11B versus $3.5B a year earlier.
threads.watch: Whether the chip and Alphabet selloff continues Monday and whether other PC or memory-exposed firms repeat Intel's warning.

threads.title: Palantir's blowout quarter and enterprise AI demand
threads.now: Palantir's third-quarter revenue rose 96% to $2.313B, its first quarter above $2B. GAAP net income was $1.128B, adjusted free cash flow $1.216B. U.S. commercial revenue grew 148% and now exceeds U.S. government revenue for the first time. Next-quarter revenue guidance is $2.649B to $2.653B.
threads.changed: Palantir reported Q3 on Nov 2: revenue $2.313B, up 96% year over year and 20% sequentially; U.S. commercial up 148%, passing government revenue for the first time.
threads.watch: Market reaction when trading opens, and whether the guidance of about $2.65B holds; no call transcript was available yet.

evidence.speaker: Alex Karp, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Palantir Technologies
evidence.quote: Our U.S. commercial revenue has surpassed our U.S. government revenue for the first time in our company's history.

history.change: Palantir Q3: revenue $2.313B (+96%), GAAP net income $1.128B, U.S. commercial +148%, guidance about $2.65B.

threads.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and the fight for the frontier
threads.now: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on Alphabet's earnings call. Relays put it first on Artificial Analysis v5.0 at 59 versus 58 for Claude Opus 5.5, and first on Mercor's APEX-Agents. A relay reports intro API pricing of $2 and $10 per million tokens, rising to $4 and $20. Access is still gated to cyber defenders. Genie 4 adds audio.
threads.changed: On AI Explained, the host said SemiAnalysis's Dylan Patel publicly apologized to Google after GDPx put Carbon second to Opus 5.5 at about a third of the cost.
threads.watch: Broader Carbon availability, confirmation of pricing on a Google page, independent evals, lab responses to GDPx grading, and Genie 4 API access.

evidence.label: Alphabet earnings call
evidence.quote: And with Gemini 4 Argon and now Carbon, which we announced today, we're excited to be leading at the frontier.

history.change: Gemini 4 Carbon announced; tops Artificial Analysis v5 and APEX-Agents per relays; access still gated to cyber defenders.

threads.title: Marvell's deal for Lumentum and the shift to optical AI connectivity
threads.now: Marvell announced with its fiscal third-quarter results that it will combine with optical maker Lumentum, expecting over $1B of run-rate synergies. Reportedly it is all stock at 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, about $115B, closing in 2028. Both CEOs cite a $550B interconnect market. Terms come from one trader's posts.
threads.changed: Reported terms: about 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, valuing Lumentum near $115B, closing in 2028. Marvell reportedly closed down 12.7% and Lumentum down 18.6%. Single-source on terms.
threads.watch: Merger 8-K and joint proxy: exchange ratio, breakup fee, antitrust review; whether Coherent and other optics names reprice as targets.

evidence.speaker: Matt Murphy, Chairman and CEO of Marvell
evidence.quote: AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation

threads.title: AI-era security: stolen API keys, AI-built exploits and misalignment tests
threads.now: Wiz reportedly counts nine AI developer platforms breached in October for stored API keys, including Northflank. Epoch reportedly found open-weight GLM-5.3 built Firefox exploits for about $1,000 each. A security guest on The Cognitive Revolution said agentic attacks now cost cents per company. Cursor's marketplace carried a tampered Claude Code extension.

threads.title: Labs claim AI-made math and physics discoveries; experts hold back
threads.now: OpenAI announced three model-produced results, including a claimed disproof of the Exponential Time Hypothesis. Reviewers Impagliazzo, Paturi and Williams say in an open letter that their involvement is not certification. A similar Anthropic 3-SAT paper is reported only secondhand.
threads.changed: Lex Fridman's math guests and MLST's Kevin Hartnett discuss the AI math wave; MLST says Epoch's test had a pre-release OpenAI model prove Erdos problem 126 and disprove 74, both checked in Lean.
threads.watch: An expert verdict on the ETH result, the KITP Yang-Mills group statement, and a first-party Anthropic post.

history.change: ETH disproof reviewers disclaim certification; verdict still pending.
Lex Fridman and MLST transcripts add context: Lean-checked Erdos results, guests favouring human-AI collaboration over AI-only maths.

threads.title: Mistral Large 4: a trillion-parameter open model and the open-versus-closed compute gap
threads.now: Mistral says it open-sourced Large 4, its largest open model: about one trillion parameters, sparse mixture of experts. On the Artificial Analysis coding subset it claims a tie with GLM 5.3 using half the tokens. Hosts said it trained on about 3,800 Blackwell GPUs, far below frontier clusters.
threads.changed: On The Cognitive Revolution, a Mistral researcher said Large 4 is its best agentic model and the best open model on coding, tied with GLM 5.3 at half the tokens. The claims are Mistral's own.
threads.watch: Independent evals of Large 4, its licence and hosting terms, and whether Western enterprises adopt it over Chinese open models.

history.change: Mistral Large 4 open release discussed on The Cognitive Revolution: one trillion parameters, claimed tie with GLM 5.3 on coding at half the tokens.
